results.name: Back and Forward Leg Swings
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and use a nearby support (such as a squat cage, wall or a chair) for balance.
Swing your right leg forward and backward in a controlled, rhythmic manner.
After completing the desired number of swings with your right leg, switch to your left leg and repeat the movement.
Focus on smooth and controlled swings, avoiding excessive momentum.
tips: Focus on maintaining a steady rhythm to ensure controlled movements.
Ensure your upper body remains upright and avoid leaning forward or backward.
Keep your supporting leg slightly bent to enhance balance and reduce strain on your joints.
results.description: Back and Forward Leg Swings is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Quadriceps.

results.name: Ball Headlock Squat
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold an exercise ball to your side with one arm wrapped around it as if in a headlock. Extend the opposite arm in front of you for balance.
Begin lowering into a squat by bending your hips and knees, keeping your chest upright and back straight.
Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor and then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the ball securely pressed to your side to maintain upper body control and tension.
Use your extended arm for balance and avoid shifting your torso.
Do not let your knees cave inward and keep them in line with your toes.
results.description: Ball Headlock Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Abdominals.

results.name: Band Cross Abduction
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and place the resistance band under both feet, crossing the band in front of you. Hold the handles of the band in opposite hands with arms hanging in front of your hips.
Keeping your right leg straight, lift it sideways away from your body until your leg is fully extended to the side.
Slowly lower your leg back to the starting position with control, keeping tension in the band.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under your feet and properly crossed to avoid slipping.
Keep your upper body stationary and avoid leaning to the side.
Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Band Cross Abduction is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abductors.

results.name: Band Hip Adduction
instructions: Secure one end of the resistance band to a stable anchor and attach the other end around the ankle closest to the anchor.
Stand sideways to the anchor with your supporting leg slightly bent and your core engaged. Place your hands on hips for stability.
Sweep the banded leg inward across the front of your body while keeping your torso upright and your movement controlled.
Slowly return your leg to the starting position without letting the band pull it back, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning to either side.
Maintain a slight bend in your supporting knee for better stability. Keep the working leg straight or slightly bent throughout the movement.
Control the return phase and resist the band's pull. Use a resistance level that allows a full, controlled range of motion.
Exhale as you bring your leg inward and inhale as you return.
results.description: Band Hip Adduction is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Glutes, Core.

results.name: Band Leg Press
instructions: Attach a resistance band at a low-mid point on sturdy equipment. Lie on your back facing the extended cable passing over your torso, and attach your right ankle to the band using a cuff.
Bend your right knee and pull it toward your chest, while the other leg stays extended and relaxed on the floor.
Press your foot forward against the resistance, straightening your leg fully without locking the knee.
Return slowly to the starting position. Repeat for the desired repetitions, switch legs, and repeat.
tips: Engage your core to stabilize your body during the motion.
Adjust your body’s distance from the anchor to maintain consistent tension.
Ensure the band or cable has tension at the start of the movement.
results.description: Band Leg Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Band Pullthrough
instructions: Stand facing away from the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart and the resistance band passing between your legs, held securely with both hands in front of you. Keep your knees slightly bent and your spine neutral.
Push your hips back while hinging at the hips, allowing your hands to move between your legs as the band stretches. Maintain a flat back and keep your arms extended.
Drive your hips forward by squeezing your glutes and return to a fully upright position while keeping your arms straight and the band under tension.
Pause briefly at the top with your glutes fully contracted, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your spine neutral and avoid rounding your back throughout the movement.
Focus on hinging at the hips rather than squatting down.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees throughout the exercise.
results.description: Band Pullthrough is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Core.

results.name: Band Spanish Split Squat
instructions: Stand in a split stance with your left leg forward and the other leg behind you, facing sturdy equipment. Loop a resistance band around your left leg, just under the knee, and anchor it in front of you at knee level.
Hold your hands together in front of your chest and keep your torso upright.
Lower your body straight down by bending both knees until your left thigh is parallel to the floor.
Push through the heel of your left foot to return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired repetitions, switch legs, and repeat.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward during the movement.
Drive through the heel of your front foot for better glute and quad engagement.
Adjust the band tension before starting to ensure proper resistance.
Inhale as you lower and exhale as you stand.
results.description: Band Spanish Split Squat is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Abdominals.

results.name: Banded Feet Elevated Hip Thrusters
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms by your sides and your heels placed on an elevated surface such as a bench or box. Wrap a resistance band just above your knees to add extra glute activation.
Bend your knees at approximately 90 degrees and keep your feet hip-width apart. Brace your core and maintain a neutral spine.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips off the ground by contracting your glutes, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your knees at the top.
Pause at the top while pushing your knees slightly outward against the band, then lower your hips back to the ground in a controlled motion. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band stays under consistent tension throughout the movement.
Drive through your heels to maximize glute activation.
Do not let your legs cave inward; push them outward against the band.
Exhale as you lift your hips, and inhale as you lower your hips.
results.description: Banded Feet Elevated Hip Thrusters is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Quadriceps, Abductors.

results.name: Barbell Bench Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, back facing a bench, holding a barbell across your upper back. Your hands should grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your chest up. Begin the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, lowering your body until you sit down on the bench.
Push through your heels to stand back up to the starting position, extending your hips and knees fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your knees track over your toes to prevent knee injuries and ensure proper form.
Keep your chest up and back straight throughout the movement to maintain proper alignment.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
results.description: Barbell Bench Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

results.name: Barbell Box Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, back facing a sturdy box. Position a barbell across your upper back, gripping it with both hands, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Slowly lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back, keeping your back straight.
Lower yourself until your glutes lightly touch the box or bench. Ensure your knees track over your toes and do not cave inward.
Push through your heels to stand back up to the starting position, extending your hips and knees fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your knees track over your toes to prevent knee injuries and ensure proper form.
Lower your body slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
results.description: Barbell Box Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.
